yt.title: How GPS knows where you are #Shorts
yt.description:
A 30-second look at how satellite navigation works.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.text: How does GPS know where you are?
scenes.narration: Your phone has no idea where it is... until it checks the time. GPS is a timing problem.
Each GPS satellite continuously broadcasts its position and the exact time the signal was sent.
Radio waves travel at the speed of light, so the delay of the signal tells your phone how far away the satellite is.
In one billionth of a second, light travels about thirty centimeters. So the clocks have to be extremely precise.
scenes.label: Light in 1 billionth of a second

scenes.narration: Three satellites are enough to fix a position in space. A fourth lets the receiver correct its own cheap clock.
